paper.title: On the Low-Complexity of Fair Learning for Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial multi-armed bandit with fairness constraints
unmapped: Each arm n must receive at least average reward lambda_n (known to the learner); feasibility with slack delta > 0 (Slater-type condition)
Collection of feasible super arms S is known and may be exponentially large; regret is against the optimal stationary randomized policy over S satisfying the fairness constraints with slack delta
settings.definition_quote: We consider a combinatorial multi-armed bandit with $N$ arms, allowing for the simultaneous selection of multiple arms in each round. ... $\{X_n(t)\}_{t\geq0}$ are i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables with an unknown mean $\mu_n\in(0,1]$. ... ensures fairness among arms through guaranteeing each arm $n$ to receive at least the reward $\lambda_n>0$ on average ... $\text{Reg}(T) \triangleq \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu_n(\bE[S^*_n]-\bE[S_n(t)])$

bound.expression: Min(K*T/(eta*mu_min) + 2*sqrt(6*K*m*T*log(T)) + K*(1 + 5*pi**2/12) + 2*C_1*K*T/eta + C_2*K*pi**2/6 + (1 + log(T))/C_3*K*log(m*T/K) + C_2*K + (1 + log(T))*sqrt(6*K*m*T*log(T))/(2*C_3), m*mu_max*T)
bound.expression_latex: \min \bigg\{ \frac{NT}{\eta\mu_{\min}} +2\sqrt{6NS_{\max}T\log T} +N(1+\frac{5\pi^2}{12}) + \frac{2C_1(M) NT}{\eta} + C_2(M) \frac{N\pi^2}{6} + \frac{1+\log T}{C_3(M)}N\log \frac{S_{\max}T}{N} + C_2(M) N + \frac{(1+\log T)\sqrt{6NS_{\max}T\log T}}{2C_3(M)}, S_{\max}\mu_{\max}T \bigg\}

symbols.alpha_M: M/|S|, M = number of randomly picked super arms per round, |S| = number of feasible super arms

conditions: fairness constraints feasible with slack delta > 0

source.label: prop:regret
source.quote: [Cumulative Regret] Under the \lc{} algorithm with $\epsilon\leq \delta/2$, the cumulative regret $\text{Reg}(T)$ over consecutive $T$ rounds can be bounded from above as follows: ... where $C_1(M)\triangleq (\alpha^2(M)-3\alpha(M)+2)/\alpha^2(M)$, $C_2(M)\triangleq 1/\alpha(M) -1$ and $C_3(M)\triangleq -\log (1-\alpha(M))$.

results.notes: Paper's N (number of base arms) mapped to K; S_max (max super-arm size) mapped to m. Regret against optimal stationary randomized fair policy. Horizon: algorithm uses log t, but eta may be tuned with T (e.g. eta = sqrt(T)); marked anytime for the stated bound with fixed eta. Proposition number inferred from separate proposition counter.

symbols.eps_q: virtual-queue parameter epsilon of the algorithm
symbols.D: positive constant chosen so that gamma >= 1/(1+delta)

conditions: fairness constraints feasible with slack delta > 0

source.label: prop:zero_violation
source.quote: [Zero Cumulative Fairness Violations] Under the \lc{} algorithm, if $\epsilon \leq (\gamma\delta+\gamma-1)/2$, there exists a zero violation point $t_0\triangleq g_0(\eta)/\epsilon=O(\eta/\epsilon)$ after which the zero cumulative fairness violation is achieved for any round $t\geq t_0$ ...

results.notes: Bound is on the zero-violation time t_0: for all t >= t_0, sum_n (sum_{tau<t}(lambda_n - E[S_n X_n]))^+ = 0. N mapped to K.

cited_results.cited_title: An efficient pessimistic-optimistic algorithm for stochastic linear bandits with general constraints
cited_results.setting_description: CMAB / linear bandits with fairness (general) constraints; regret with zero cumulative constraint violation after some rounds
